truthBoundaries: Hosted Python source validation proves the Python, shell, workflow and policy contract only; it does not prove that Docker, Godot or .NET exists on a runner.
A headless import does not prove visual quality, input, game feel or a complete playthrough.
A bounded boot proves startup only.
A recorded movie, screenshot set or contact sheet is visual evidence, not a complete playthrough.
Synthetic keyboard and mouse events prove the declared Godot input path, not physical-device latency.
Synthetic joypad events prove InputMap coverage and Godot event handling, not physical USB enumeration, Steam Input, rumble or controller certification.
UI geometry telemetry detects deterministic clipping, overlap, focus and target-size defects but does not replace human art direction, accessibility or UX approval.
Xvfb and Mesa software rendering do not prove hardware-specific Vulkan behavior or performance.
Godot 4 C# projects require the .NET editor and cannot use the browser export path.
Deterministic bot exploration is bounded and does not prove every gameplay state is reachable.
Fresh-process synthetic input does not certify physical controllers, accessibility, game feel or human visual quality.
Retained audio metrics and previews support debugging but do not replace human mix, music, dialogue or spatial-audio judgment.
The MCP bridge is restricted to configured target and evidence roots and does not grant target-repository write authority.
Managed engine provisioning downloads official archives at runtime; Git does not carry platform binaries.
The engine lock governs stable branches, but a repository-owned profile may require an explicit compatible version.
A managed editor receipt and payload digest prove the provisioned files, not GPU or gameplay correctness.
A local sandbox image build may use network access to fetch checksum-verified official assets; the resulting game execution uses --network none.

Plural-localization validation proves only the exact requested CSV import and reviewed integer lookup probes at the exact target Git head; it does not grant linguistic approval, source repair, target mutation, release publication or broad locale correctness.
notes: Python 3.11.15 is exact for hosted Linux self-validation; native Windows Python remains a freshly probed 3.11.x runner capability.
Direct build and development dependencies are pinned, but their transitive graph is review-first until requirements.lock is separately generated and validated.
No source-only validation result authorises target mutation, deployment, store publication, credential change or a physical-controller or human-UX pass claim.
The optional agent extra pins mcp==1.28.1; the core Godot validation and media runtime remains dependency-free.
Docker is optional for native Windows testing but required for local no-network Linux sandbox runs.

The canonical plural-localization command is godot-lab-localization-plural, routed to the guarded localization_plural_runtime_cli facade; older direct modules are compatibility surfaces and not publication authority.
